/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
# one-step walk-forward MAE for completed FY2018-FY2025 using simple candidates
values = {
2016:304.73324693893,
2017:327.99094991796,
2018:365.93750125511,
2019:391.33399287289,
2020:431.8836721523,
2021:395.33270939953,
2022:424.5124141128,
2023:467.27343559916,
2024:456.94550440091,
2025:501.54351323803,
}
for name in ['persistence','mean_change','recent3_mean_change']:
    errors=[]
    rows=[]
    for y in range(2018,2026):
        hist=[values[k] for k in sorted(values) if k<y]
        hist_years=[k for k in sorted(values) if k<y]
        if name=='persistence': pred=values[y-1]
        elif name=='mean_change': pred=values[y-1]+sum(values[hist_years[i]]-values[hist_years[i-1]] for i in range(1,len(hist_years)))/(len(hist_years)-1)
        else:
            ch=[values[hist_years[i]]-values[hist_years[i-1]] for i in range(1,len(hist_years))]
            pred=values[y-1]+sum(ch[-3:])/min(3,len(ch))
        err=values[y]-pred
        errors.append(abs(err)); rows.append((y,pred,values[y],err))
    print(name, 'MAE', round(sum(errors)/len(errors),3), 'rows', [(y, round(p,1), round(a,1), round(e,1)) for y,p,a,e in rows])
PY"

item.text: The simple model check favors a trend/mean-change rule over pure persistence on the completed FY2016-FY2025 history: mean-change MAE is 24.1B versus 33.4B for persistence in one-step backtests. Because the target is FY2027 and FY2026 is not completed yet, I’m treating the trend rule as the benchmark and using the current FY2026 API response only as partial-year context.
